name: Rose Hermosa
lede: Rose Hermosa is a strong, warm pink first recorded by Maerz and Paul in 1930, and in our archive it turns up in only two paintings, both French portraits.

sections.title: A strong pink, rarely used
sections.body:
Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary dates Rose Hermosa to 1905, printed on their plate 1 F 8, and the Inter-Society Color Council's 1955 census files it as a strong pink, Munsell 4.3R 7.9/6.8 [1]. ColorHub's own color-distance data puts its closest learnable neighbor at [[melon]], about 4.2 units away, with [[baby-pink]] a little further at 6.6 [1].

Two other library pinks sit nearly as close: [[light-pink]] and [[pastel-pink]], each within six units [1]. The word *hermosa* is Spanish for beautiful, paired here with the flower word *rose*, though none of the sources in our library say who made that pairing or when [1]. It ranks 1,742nd of roughly 2,000 names in ColorHub's library by use[1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this pink in just 2 of 23,781 paintings, as photographed [2]. Both are French portraits painted a half-century apart: Louis Gustave Ricard's *Portrait de l'artiste* of 1853 and André Derain's *Woman in a Chemise* of 1906, and in each the color reads as a highlight, never a shadow [2]. At under a quarter of either canvas, it is an accent, not a field [2]. The counts are a computed color match on varnished, photographed canvases, never a pigment identification [2].
